sections: 2026-09-08 order: 1 pressure · 2 door · 3 map · 4 ladder · 5 next move · 6 plans · 7 bill · 8 who pays · 9 world · 10 under the war · 11 endings · 12 whispers

1.plain: All four pots sit under the 80° valve at Sunday 07:00 and none moved from 03:00: Iran 70° (6.1 — the rial slid another 300 to 236,100), the United States 79° (6.9, a second run one tick under the valve on the election clock, Brent unchanged with the market shut), Small Gulf 69° (6.0), Saudi–UAE 59° (5.2, eighth run; the Sep 25 crossing down still held). The day's points are written plain. What arrived by midday Tehran was a claim, not fire: the Guards' navy says it captured a second American underwater drone — a Remus 600 — 'in a coordinated and complex operation'. Washington has said nothing, which on the Sep 8 precedent (the first capture confirmed by CENTCOM within hours) is itself worth watching; a confirmation would go to the ladder at rung 4 for the house's tick, but it is not fire and moves no pot. The army chief's full text — 'if Iran can't live, no one can trade and live' — and the IRGC Navy's 'even in the Indian Ocean' are words. The export counter showed its first barrels in seven days, all petrochemicals.
1.trade: Tonight's 22:00 UTC open has a new item to price and it is small: a claimed seizure of an American survey robot in the strait, unconfirmed, no ship involved — the kind of thing that adds a dollar if CENTCOM confirms and nothing if it doesn't. The larger facts stand from Friday: a public 'no' with a map, answered by 'only a negotiated solution' and 'won't soften'; a sanctions coalition the Treasury says is 'delivering results' with Iraq now negotiating an exemption; and a door that is measurably a trickle — 5 in / 13 out, the counter's first 134,653 barrels in a week all petrochemicals, Windward's 19 million barrels of Sep 24 outflow two-thirds ship-to-ship. Five satellite passes show nothing massing at Bushehr or Bandar Abbas. The US pot is one tick from the valve on the calendar alone; a firmer open does it, and a crossing up would be held for the house exactly as the crossing down was.

2.plain: The door closed Thursday at 12 in / 11 out with 76 hulls inside, and by 22:00 UTC Friday had three in and nine out with 71 inside — the in-strait count rose through the evening, the crossings did not. The 24-hour log has an LNG tanker and a bulker out and a bulker, an LPG and a small products tanker in — nothing crude-sized either way — and the export counter sat at 0 bbl all day. Reuters' preliminary count was nine transits on Thursday against a ten-day average of about 18; Al Arabiya's data story says traffic is still below that average. That is the measured door. Against it, a US official now says 40 million barrels moved in 48 hours 'under US escort' — the third telling of Wednesday's sixty ships, still with no CENTCOM release and no AIS echo; PortWatch, stuck at Sep 20, will say.
2.trade: Each week under 10 transits/day has lifted Brent; creditor selling steepens the curve.

3.plain: Carriers hold outside Iran's 300 km ring; the fight is inside it. USNI Sep 14: both carriers and the Boxer group in the Arabian Sea, no US warship named inside the Gulf; Ross back with Bush.
3.trade: A carrier inside the ring is the tell for a wider war.

4.plain: Fifty items wait for the house's tick and NOTHING new was held at Sep 27 07:00. The candidate that mattered was the Guards' claim to have captured a second American underwater drone (Remus 600) in the strait — Statement No. 17 via Fars and state TV, relayed by AFP — and the referee kept it off the ladder because it is one region's word: no CENTCOM statement, no Western confirmation, no position, no picture. The rule is explicit (unconfirmed claims wait in the weak column), and the precedent is Sep 8, when CENTCOM confirmed the first capture the same day and the event went to rung 4; if that happens again the next run proposes rung 4 for the tick. It is not fire, so 'fired' and the pots are untouched. The army chief's full text, Mohammadi's Indian Ocean line and the export counter's first barrels are logged as rechecks and weak rows; the referee flagged, an eighth time, that the US table cannot score the rejection and the Iran table cannot score a threat short of fire — or, now, the seizure of American unmanned equipment. Seven rechecks written; the Sep 27 forecast frozen unchanged.
4.trade: A confirmed pipeline hit is the rung-7 print that re-prices Brent; watch for a rung-9 act (a US warship actually hit) or the first rung-10 act since February.

5.plain: Most likely next 14 days (Sep 27 freeze, window to Oct 11): Iran seizes or fires on a tanker (41%); a Gulf energy strike is the second card (30%); the Houthis on the Red Sea third; a US warship hit 14%. US: sink more Iranian tankers 53%, bigger escorted convoys 39%, a pause that blesses the corridor third. The posteriors have not moved since Sep 11 because every signal since then is held for the house's tick. Scorecard after five graded days: 10 calls, 6 hits, Brier 0.141; next grade Oct 1 (the Sep 17 freeze).
5.trade: Tanker rates and war-risk premia up; XLE over SPX; long-dated Brent calls cheap if force-scenario odds are right.

6.plain: Iran wants to force an escalation before Nov 3; the US wants to squeeze and hold.
6.trade: No deal premium: fade rallies on 'talks' headlines unless a convoy actually transits.

7.plain: America's quiet bill, Wednesday close posted Friday: the ten-year at 5.18% and the thirty-year at 5.47% (Sep 24, FRED) — seven basis points above the Sep 23 closes, which were already the highest since 2007 and 2004; gas $4.478; foreign official custody of Treasuries down $11.4B on the week to $2,597.5B, the third fall in four weeks and about $145B below end-April. Iran's parliament speaker is keeping score in public ('Happy 5.1% 10Y America'). The Senate declined, 49-50, to make the war the president's problem before Nov 3 — so the bill stays his.
7.trade: Bear-steepener with official selling: a custody week of +$30B after an intervention has marked the local top in yields twice (Jul 29, Aug 26) — this week was -$11B, so no top signal. DXY firm short-term (safe haven), soft long-term (reserve share).

8.plain: Iran and the small Gulf states pay; Israel doesn't.
8.trade: Qatar and Kuwait sovereign spreads wider; Israeli equities unaffected.

9.plain: Russia and Egypt win; Asia's importers lose; creditors trim.
9.trade: Long RUB oil revenue proxies; short INR/JPY on oil-import stress.

10.plain: The engine (lobby, arms, oil) still beats the brake (voters) — but the gap is closing.
10.trade: LMT/RTX hold while engine ≥8; first brake-over-engine print is the sell signal.

11.plain: Bigger war 33%, Stuck 31%, Strait regime 17%, Signed deal 8%, Regime change 6%.
11.trade: Bigger-war above 30% is the level to hedge with long-dated Brent calls; Signed deal above 20% is the level for Brent < $85.

12.plain: Weak signals: whether CENTCOM confirms, denies or ignores the Guards' second underwater-drone claim (a confirmation = rung 4 for the tick; silence past 48 h = withdrawn); whether the mediators' 'definitive positions' reach Tehran and what they say; whether five top-level threats in two days (Hatami, Mohammadi, Akraminia, Haji-Babaei, Statement No. 17's 'the strait is closed') precede an act against a ship — the first in five days would end the quiet; whether the counter's first petrochemical barrels are followed by a crude-sized hull outbound; whether the Saudi–Houthi exchange draws a fourth salvo (none in 36 h) now that Paris has called its deployment 'strictly defensive'; whether Baghdad gets its exemption and whether the Iraqi street matters to it; tonight's 22:00 UTC Brent open against a US pot one tick under the valve; Monday's USNI tracker and whether the two carriers have moved.

tiles.counter: one scale for every pot: 100° = boils over (a side gives up its aim); 80° = the emergency valve, past which a side is forced to escalate and acts against its own interest. Underneath, every pot shares one trigger on the 0–10 score — 7.0, the valve (re-fit monthly, the same for all four); the display maps 7.0 to 80° and 10 to 100°, so a degree means the same thing in every pot and the gap from 80° to 100° is a side's remaining tolerance

tiles.counter: definitions: Stuck = no signed deal, no regime change, door under 30 ships/day, fighting continues; Signed deal = a signed US–Iran agreement (not an MOU, not a pause); Regime change = any leadership change in Tehran, including an IRGC takeover or Khamenei succession; Bigger war = US or Israeli strikes on Iranian territory sustained over a week, or a Gulf-wide exchange, or US ground forces engaged; Strait regime = passage resumes ≥30 ships/day under Iran–Oman rules or fees, no war, no signed deal; Other = anything else (Houthi Red Sea closure, US unilateral pause, etc.)

tiles.counter: AIS shows only ships that broadcast — dark tankers and most warships are invisible; ADS-B shows only aircraft with transponders on — military aircraft over Iran do not broadcast, so an empty sky is 'not seen', not 'not there'. Dead-reckoned positions are extrapolations, not fixes. Thermal anomalies cannot say what burned or who lit it
tiles.source: Live layer: every AIS commercial ship from hormuz.data-tracking.net /api/ships (MarineTraffic feeds, 30-min polls) and every ADS-B aircraft from adsb.lol (four 250-nm circles) — rebuilt every 10 minutes by a GitHub Action (live.json) and, between fixes, moved along last course and speed (dead reckoning, ≤20 min). Basemap: NASA VIIRS true colour via GIBS, newest complete pass (date on the toggle). Fire dots: VIIRS 375 m thermal anomalies, last 48 h (flares are normal; a new dot at a port, refinery or base is the signal). US warship positions: USNI Fleet & Marine Tracker (weekly, Monday) — the tracker names the sea, the point inside it is ours (JUDGMENT); roster as of Sep 8: George Washington + George H.W. Bush CSGs and the Boxer ARG in the Arabian Sea, Lincoln departed for Thailand Sep 2 · Satellite checks (S badges): Sentinel-2 via GIBS, 30 m, latest cloud-free pass per site, vessel counts at pier/anchor are our reading (JUDGMENT)

tiles.counter: These are correlations with the war window, not attributions: Korea and Malaysia are riding the AI-chip cycle, China's record exports are partly tariff front-running and a weak yuan, Brazil's crude surge started before March. Russia's beat is Q2 y/y against a weak 2025 base and its budget oil take is still falling. Most trade prints are one month; Q2 GDP is preliminary and gets revised.
tiles.moves: Monthly: China customs (~7th), Korea MOTIE (1st), Brazil MDIC (1st week), Malaysia DOSM (~20th), Russian MinFin oil & gas revenue (3rd). Quarterly: Q3 GDP prints late Oct (Korea, China) and Nov (Russia, Brazil). IMF October WEO replaces the July forecast column.
tiles.source: Scoreboard = latest official prints, not forecasts: Rosstat Q2 GDP (Aug 12), Bank of Russia balance of payments (Jan–May goods surplus, Q2 current account), MinFin monthly oil & gas revenue and H1 deficit; China NBS Q2 GDP / Jul activity / PPI-CPI (Aug 17) and General Administration of Customs August trade (Sep 8); Korea MOTIE August trade (Sep 1), Bank of Korea Q2 advance GDP and GDI, KRX H1 operating profit, SK hynix 2Q26; Brazil IBGE Q2 GDP, MDIC monthly trade, BCB Focus survey; Malaysia DOSM July trade (Aug 20), MITI, IMF WEO Jul 2026 for the growth forecast. Export-engine bars: same customs/ministry releases; Russia surplus = Jan–May monthly average; ringgit at 4.2 RM/$.
tiles.trade: The trade is not Russia or China — it is the AI-hardware exporters (Korea, Malaysia, Taiwan) and non-Gulf crude exporters (Brazil) that carry a war premium without war exposure; China gets export volume but no domestic lift; Russia gets prices and a current-account cushion but not budget cash.
